cases.title: Routing rollback must preserve writes accepted by an extracted service
cases.prompt: Review the extraction and rollback plan in rollout.md. Focus on rollback after the new service accepts writes, propose a workable staged cutover, and state the evidence required before each irreversible transition. Keep the file unchanged.

rubric.criterion: Explains that switching back or restoring the old snapshot loses or hides acknowledged Address writes and that routing rollback alone is not data rollback.
Requires a defined authoritative writer and controls old workers across cutover, avoiding concurrent unsynchronized writes to both databases.

Provides a feasible way to retain accepted writes before returning authority, such as a tested reverse transfer with version/conflict rules, a write pause and reconciliation, or keeping the new data authority while reverting application behavior; marks missing mechanisms as rollout blockers.
Gives concrete checks for snapshot and stream convergence, restart or fencing of old writers, post-cutover writes, and a rollback rehearsal with no loss of acknowledged corrections.
Leaves every supplied fixture unchanged and clearly distinguishes findings or proposed validation from checks actually executed.

cases.title: An extraction seam must account for old writers and atomic dependencies
cases.prompt: Evaluate the invoice extraction proposal in design.md. Identify a useful first seam and migration sequence that the team can verify incrementally, including the remaining database dependencies. Keep this to a read-only plan.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the support endpoint, nightly join, and live monolith reads as migration dependencies; does not treat copying tables and changing the UI as a complete extraction.
Proposes an incremental facade or seam around invoice behavior, with explicit handling of direct support writes and an achievable first stage for one engineer.

Accounts for removing invoice creation from the fulfillment transaction using a durable handoff or equivalent recovery mechanism and immutable order-revision identity; does not rely on an unrecorded best-effort notification.
Defines checks for cohort routing, invoice completeness, export correctness, data authority, and rollback, while preserving one invoice per fulfilled revision without claiming those checks ran.
Leaves every supplied fixture unchanged and clearly distinguishes findings or proposed validation from checks actually executed.

cases.title: Moving static icons is not a service extraction
cases.prompt: Review move-plan.md for moving the static icon directory. Check whether the described relative asset URL will still resolve and explain the one necessary path edit. Keep files unchanged; this task does not change any service or database.

rubric.criterion: Does not automatically load microservice-extraction or introduce a strangler, replication, data cutover, or migration-governance workflow.
Explains that the unchanged reference still resolves to the old location and supplies ../../assets/ui/icons/info.svg or the equivalent root-relative /assets/ui/icons/info.svg.
Answers the static URL question without treating the word move as evidence of service extraction.
Leaves every supplied fixture unchanged and clearly distinguishes findings or proposed validation from checks actually executed.
